newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to restructure, privatise energy sector.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to restructure, privatise energy sector.

text.p: Ukraine plans to transform its state-run oil and gas sectors into privatised, vertically integrated companies, an industry source said on Thursday.
Stepan Yaloveha, spokesman for the State Oil and Gas Committee, said officials would complete a plan by October 15 to overhaul the former Soviet republic's energy industry.
"The idea is to set up integrated companies in different parts of Ukraine that would be responsible for the whole oil and gas process, from the beginning to the very end," Yaloveha said.
"The oil and gas industry needs structural changes. We think that this would help to increase domestic output."
He gave no time frame for the transformation.

Yaloveha said the scheme involves the creation of the vertically integrated Ukrnaftogaz company, which would include several smaller firms such as Ukrnafta, Ukrnaftaproduct and Ukrnaftokhimpererobka, all in the refining and marketing sectors.

Another company, Ukrshelfnaftogaz, would be responsible for drilling for oil and gas in the Black Sea shelf and be based in the Crimean peninsula. It would absorb Chernomornaftogaz, which currently deals with offshore oil and gas reserves.
At least three additional regional companies would be created and then partly privatised with the state's share at no less than 51 percent, Yaloheva said.
According to current estimates, Ukraine, where oil exploration has declined since the early 1970s, has oil reserves of 1.05 billion tonnes (7.7 billion barrels).
Domestic annual crude demand is 15-20 million tonnes (300,000-400 barrels per day) and Ukraine expects to import 12 million tonnes of oil this year (240,000 bpd).
Domestic annual gas output is 18.2 billion cubic metres.
Ukraine imports 66 billion cubic metres of gas from Russia and the Central Asian state of Turkmenistan.
